headline: Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson has signed a law that bars large grocery chains from setting prices using shoppers' personal data.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a first-of-its-kind local law on personalised grocery pricing, but one city's rule with an untested effect.
importance_line: Seattle shoppers should no longer be charged prices based on their personal data at big grocery chains, but the law covers one city, a grocers' group calls it untested and warns of lost discounts, and Safeway says it does not price that way.
summary: KOMO News reports that Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson signed the Fair and Transparent Pricing ordinance on 5 Oct 2026, after a 7-2 city council vote, barring grocery chains with at least 20 locations worldwide from using shoppers' personal data, browsing history, social media activity or chatbot conversations to set prices, though ordinary coupons and discounts stay allowed. The city calls it the first such law in the US, and it was partly inspired by 2025 consumer investigations, one of which found prices up to 23% apart for the same item at a single Seattle Safeway.
